items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: So the bottom line is the guy that came over to teach me was originally a studio guitarist, I believe for CBS in New York, his name was George O’Dell, he called himself George Dell

ctx.x: Okay. I heard, because I’m not from this area, I didn’t quite know you a real long time ago. I heard something about George Dell, the music store owner, visiting you when you were laid up or something, to give you a start. Is that true?

Oh yeah, yeah. What happened, as a child I had a problem with my hip. And so I was in the hospital for an extended period of time while they were finding different surgeries and therapies to try to get me to be able to walk. As a result I was in the hospital for more than three years, without going home. And this happened at the time I was between nine and eleven or something like that. So to try to give me something to do, one of my aunts brought me a little plastic ukulele and I’m sitting there figuring stuff…

he retired from professional music in New York, he came back to his wife’s home town which was Utica, and the wife used to be a nurse at what is now Faxton Hospital, then it was Children’s Hospital. So they called her and said hey, your husband teaches? You want to send him up and teach this kid we got? And so he would come up and give me a half hour lesson.
